newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV says Q1 gain explained by basic banking, Latam.
newsitem.headline: BBV says Q1 gain explained by basic banking, Latam.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya said on Thursday its 24.8 percent rise in first quarter profits stemmed in large part from earnings abroad and from basic banking business.

In a statement, Spain's second-largest bank said: "The bank's environment has been characterised by a moderate, but continuous improvement in real growth and of economic imbalances in Spain as well as in Latin America."
Pre-tax profits from BBV's Latin American groups were 10.45 billion pesetas, compared with total pre-tax profit of 57.77 billion pesetas, the statement said.
Traditional banking business also performed well.
Operating margin, which includes earnings on loans and commissions and well as own-account trading, rose 41.2 percent.
Net interest income rose 24 percent, commissions gained 35.1 percent and profit on financial operations jumped 159.9 percent.
